title: add jsonschema strict-mode with improved error messages (OpenAI compat)
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: make structured output (response_format: json_schema) more robust and developer-friendly by adding a strict mode that enforces schema conformance at the API layer, and by surfacing clearer, OpenAI-compatible error messages when validation fails. This PR implements: 1) response_format.strict_mode boolean plumbing through API surface (openai-compat layer + internal request model), 2) server-side JSON Schema validation step that runs after decoding/output normalization, 3) detailed, structured error payloads for validation failures (error_type, path, expected, received, snippet) and mapping to OpenAI-style error codes/messages for the compatibility layer, 4) SDK helper changes (python/typescript) to expose structured error enums and retry hints, 5) docs + examples + test harness updates. Checklist: - [x] Implement strict_mode flag parsing and propagation - [x] Add schema validator module with streaming-friendly validation path - [x] Produce deterministic, small error payloads for downstream clients - [x] Wire OpenAI-compat layer to return compat errors when requested - [x] Backwards-compatible: default strict_mode=false - [x] Add unit and integration tests (server + sdk + examples) - [ ] Add performance microbenchmarks (follow-up PR) Related: ENG-2183 (schema validation infra), PM-412 (structured-output roadmap).
commits_summary: a1b2c3d: wire strict_mode through request parser and API handler
d4e5f6a: add jsonschema validator with streaming-safe checks
b7c8d9e: map internal validation errors to openai-compat error responses
c0ffee1: add SDK enum and docs examples
f1f2f3a: tests + fixtures for strict and non-strict behavior
release_notes: Adds optional response_format.strict_mode for server-side JSON Schema validation; improves validation error payloads and OpenAI-compat mapping. Backwards compatible by default. SDKs expose new error enums and docs updated.
review_conversation: Marco Reyes (reviewer): Please split long error messages into a compact payload and attach a human_readable field. Also make sure we don't log full user inputs.
Aisha Patel (author): Updated mapper to return compact fields (error_type, path, expected, received, snippet) and an optional human_readable message; logs redact user content by default.

Sofia Turner (reviewer): Can we ensure streaming responses don't trigger a late validation that drops the whole response? Suggest incremental validation and best-effort partial streaming when strict_mode=false.

Aisha Patel (author): Implemented streaming-friendly validator that validates chunks where possible and performs a final conformance pass before finalizing the response. In strict_mode=true finalization will fail the request with a 400-like validation error.
Evan Murray (approver): LGTM after addressing comments about compat error codes. Approving for merge.
testing_notes: Added unit tests for validator edge cases, integration tests that exercise openai-compat mapping, and end-to-end example in examples/structured-output. CI covers server+sdk matrix on linux. Perf microbenchmarks skipped intentionally and tracked under perf:follow-up label.
notes_on_backward_compatibility: Default behavior unchanged: strict_mode is opt-in. When not set or false the validator runs in permissive mode (issues are logged but not surfaced as errors). OpenAI-compat layer only returns compat validation errors when requested via strict_mode or when client uses response_format with strict=true.
security_considerations: Validator includes size limits to avoid catastrophic memory use for large schemas/outputs and redaction of sensitive fields in error snippets. Added tests to ensure no PII is included in error payloads by default.
post_merge_actions: 1) follow-up perf microbenchmarks (ENG-3201), 2) announce feature in release notes and migration guide, 3) add more SDK helper ergonomics based on customer feedback.
changelog_entry: Added optional response_format.strict_mode (server-side JSON Schema validation) and improved OpenAI-compat error mapping. Backwards compatible by default.
maintainer_notes: Keep strict_mode off by default; monitor error rates and customer friction. If many customers adopt strict_mode, consider a follow-up opt-in telemetry flag to measure schema coverage and common failure modes.
qa_notes: QA exercised both strict_mode=true and false, validated OpenAI-compat error shapes, and confirmed SDKs surface enums. Verified that example continues to work with default settings.
